title: King Frederick shelters hermetic thinkers; Descartes fights on the other side
summary: Jesse Michels tells of King Frederick shelters hermetic thinkers; Descartes fights on the other side, about early 17th century at Bohemia / Palatinate, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talking with the philosopher Jason Jorjani, recalls a book by the historian Frances Yates called The Rosicrucian Enlightenment. Michels says it describes King Frederick, a ruler in Bohemia and the Palatinate in central Europe in the early 1600s, sheltering mystical and heretical thinkers such as John Dee, Edward Kelley and possibly Giordano Bruno, and that in the war that followed the philosopher René Descartes fought on the other side, which casts the birth of modern thought as a clash with these older mystical traditions.
